title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 16°, 'Réflexions sur le théorème de Fermat', opens here. The '7 33' at the top is the page number 733 of the Longue Marche continuation.

(1) Restatement of Fermat. For n ≥ 3, Fermat's Last Theorem says the affine Fermat curve over Q has no rational points:
U_n = {(x_0:x_1:x_∞) ∈ P^2 with all x_i invertible, x_0^n + x_1^n + x_∞^n = 0}.
Equivalently, U_n is the closed curve x_0^n + x_1^n + x_∞^n = 0 inside the 2-dimensional torus T = G_m^{{0,1,∞}}/G_m (diagonal). Here 'Γ' means the set of rational points (sections).

(2) The Fermat tower via the torus. Write T = G_{m,Q} ⊗_Z M, where M = Z^{{0,1,∞}}/Z·(1,1,1) is a rank-2 lattice. The line x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0 inside T is U_1. U_1 is P^1 minus three points, i.e. M_{0,3}. Grothendieck recalls from §11° (p. 696 ff.) and §14° that U_n is the inverse image of U_1 under the Kummer isogeny of index n, x ↦ x^n:
1 → μ_n ⊗ M → T → T → 1.
So U_n → U_1 is a Galois étale cover with group μ_n ⊗ M ≅ (μ_n)^3/μ_n, which has order n^2 (≅ (Z/n)^2 over Q̄).

(3) Genus. Let Û_n be the smooth compactification. Û_n → Û_1 ≅ P^1 has degree n^2. Above each of 0, 1, ∞ it has ramification index n, so n points lie over each cusp and 3n points at infinity in total; it is étale elsewhere. Riemann–Hurwitz, completed on the next page:
2 − 2g_n − 3n = n^2(2 − 3),
so g_n = 1 + n(n−3)/2 = (n−1)(n−2)/2.

(4) Purpose. The next page sets up an anabelian attack on Fermat. All U_n are anabelian, and Û_n is too for n ≥ 4. Granting the section conjecture, rational points of U_n correspond to sections of 1 → π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) → π_1(U_n) → Γ_Q → 1 other than the 3n cuspidal 'sections at infinity'. Grothendieck proposes to characterise these as the sections for which the centraliser of Γ_Q^+ = Ker(χ) in π_1(U_n) is trivial. The point is that π_1(U_n) sits inside π_1(U_1) = π_1(M_{0,3}) as the kernel of a map to μ_n ⊗ M. This links Fermat to the Galois action on the profinite π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which is the theme of the preceding sections (e.g. ζ_{p,ℓ} restricted to inertia).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The kernel μ_n ⊗ M has order n^2, the ramification data are right, and the genus formula obtained on the next page, g_n = 1 + n(n−3)/2, is the classical (n−1)(n−2)/2.
Minor point: 'totalement ramifié' is crossed out and replaced by 'ramification de degrés n'. The correction is right: the cover has degree n^2, so it is not totally ramified at 0, 1, ∞.

ideas.what: Fermat's Last Theorem restated as the affine Fermat curve in the torus G_m^3/G_m having no Q-points.
ideas.modern_name: Affine Fermat curve as a curve in a split torus

ideas.what: U_n is the inverse image of U_1 = P^1 − {0,1,∞} (the line x_0+x_1+x_∞=0 in T) under the n-th power Kummer isogeny of the 2-dimensional torus. This makes U_n → M_{0,3} an abelian étale cover with group μ_n ⊗ M ≅ (Z/n)^2.
ideas.modern_name: Fermat curves as (Z/n)^2 Kummer covers of P^1 − {0,1,∞}; the Fermat tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (e.g. Rohrlich on the cusps of Fermat curves); Ihara 1986 (Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications); Anderson 1989
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; the Longue Marche (1981) circulated only privately.

ideas.what: Genus of the compactified Fermat curve computed by Riemann–Hurwitz.
Plan (continued on the next page) to read Fermat as non-existence of non-cuspidal sections of the arithmetic π_1 extension of U_n, inside π_1(M_{0,3}).
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture applied to Fermat curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's section conjecture (letter to Faltings, 1983); later work on Galois action on Fermat-curve π_1 by Ihara, Anderson, and Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren
ideas.where_published: The letter to Faltings discusses anabelian approaches to Mordell; an explicit Fermat discussion there is uncertain.

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins a programme to treat FLT anabelianly. He embeds the whole Fermat tower in π_1(M_{0,3}) via torus Kummer isogenies and aims to characterise rational points as sections with trivial Γ_Q^+-centraliser. This page only sets up the geometry; the anabelian characterisation follows on the next page.
missed.quote: Le "théorème de Fermat" peut s'énoncer en disant que pour n≥3, la courbe de Fermat affine ... n'a pas de pt rat /Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Section-conjecture questions for Fermat curves are still studied, e.g. Galois action on Fermat-curve homology and π_1. The torus/Kummer framing over M_{0,3} is the standard modern one, so the page is mainly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's c.1981 anabelian view of Fermat.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is classical and correct: Fermat curves as (Z/n)^2 Kummer covers of P^1 − {0,1,∞} through the torus isogeny, plus the genus formula. The only notable feature is historical. Grothendieck explicitly turns to Fermat's theorem within the anabelian programme, before Faltings and Wiles; that substance is mostly on the following page.
transcription_corrections: The heading '7^{33}' is the page number 733 written as '7 33', not an exponent.
'dans 14°) on a vu [?] la description' — the image reads approximately 'et dans 14°) on a vu la description de U_n comme image inverse de'.
In (367) the overbrace label is T = G_{m,Q} ⊗_Z M ≅ G_{m,Q}^{{0,1,∞}}/G_{m,Q}; the transcription matches.
Insertion above the ramification phrase: 'de degrés n' and 'au-dessus de' are added above 'les pts ... 0,1,∞'; 'avec' replaces a crossed-out 'totalement'.
